name: Apricot and peach oil freckle removal

image.caption: Apricot and peach oil freckle removal

lead: Apricot and peach oil freckle removal is a folk practice described as traditional in Korean beauty culture, in which oils pressed from apricot or peach kernels are applied to the skin to fade freckles and spots.
Practitioners aim for a more even complexion. Freckles themselves are clusters of concentrated melanin, so any fading would come from changes in pigmentation.

paras: The oils are applied topically as carrier oils. Results are described anecdotally and the pigment usually returns with sun exposure.

Wikipedia warns that apricot kernels contain amygdalin, which releases cyanide, and that eating them can be fatal; topical use is a different matter. Freckles can reappear after treatment if skin is not protected from the sun, and a dermatologist can identify spots that are not benign.

chain: Apply kernel oil to freckles or spots
angle.text: Users hope the oils fade freckles and spots to give an even complexion. The lightening effect is a claim made by practitioners.

lead: Apricot and peach oil freckle removal refers to the use of oils from apricot or peach kernels, described as a traditional Korean remedy, to lighten freckles and age spots. [1]
Freckles are clusters of concentrated melanin that become darker with UV exposure, and they are linked to MC1R gene variants. [2] No published trials were identified testing these oils on freckles.
infobox: Apricot kernel oil, peach kernel oil

paras: The kernels of apricot are a by-product of fruit processing, and the oil is also used in food flavoring. [1] Wikipedia notes that the kernel contains amygdalin, which breaks down to cyanide; in 2016 the European Food Safety Authority said three small bitter kernels, or half a large one, would exceed safe amygdalin levels. [1]

Wikipedia says freckles result from overproduction of melanin by melanocytes, are darkened by UV-B, and can reappear after creams or lasers if skin is not protected from the sun. [2] Freckles became fashionable in the West after the mid-20th century. [2]
